item.title: How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident
item.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. All six victims were burnt beyond recognition,” the statement said. Vanguard News The post How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
item.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. She thanked the centre’s partners and funders, assuring that it would continue to provide compassionate care where survivors’ voices mattered. item.title: 18.3m children out of school: Stakeholders demand urgent action
item.description: … NGE challenges govt, media, private sector as UNICEF warns on first 1,000 days By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners yesterday called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million children out of school in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF Representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. item.title: Security chiefs hail IGP Disu for suspending declaration of Obaigbena, others wanted
item.description: By Emma Nnadozie THE police order suspending the wanted declaration on Arise TV owner, Mr. Nduka Obaigbena and seven others over alleged assassination attempt by Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Olohundare Jimoh, has elicited reactions from some security chiefs in the country, who said that the wanted declaration was done without due process. One of the security chiefs who spoke with Vanguard, said: “It was misappropriate and procedurally flawed” and showered encomiums on the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his quick response by suspending the wanted declaration The Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Zone 2, Onikan, Lagos, Olohundare Jimoh, last Tuesday, declared Chairman of Arise News and This Day Media Group, Chief Nduka Obaigbena, Managing Director of Nestoil, Dr. Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi, and seven others wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu in a crowed press conference in Lagos. He said the declaration followed an investigation into the delivery of a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition to Alebiosu’s residence in Lagos. However, in a swift reaction two days later, the IGP, through the Force Public Relations Officer, FPRO, Ani Iniedu suspended the wanted declaration against the suspects and stated that the case has been transferred to the Force Intelligence Department, FID, Abuja, for a thorough and impartial investigation. He also directed the nine individuals to report to the FID, at the Force headquarters , Abuja, between November 26 and 30, 2026. In his reaction, the Director-General of the Institute of Security, Nigeria at the University of Lagos, Mr. Adebayo Akinade, said that the Zone 2 declaration was “misappropriate and procedurally flawed. The IGP’s suspension and transfer to Force Intelligence Department was correct, strategic and has restored public confidence.” Former Director with the Department of State Service, DSS, and currently a security consultant, Mr. Mike Ejiofor, said: “The IGP has the superior order on such matters. When a subordinate makes a mistake, the IGP is in a position to correct it. So, I do not see any conflict in the matter.” In his response the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of Perfect Security Services Limited, Dr. Patrick Uwagbale saw the incident as “part of a system that is not in order. A good society will do something according to the rules. Even if the allegation is true or not, it is unheard of that someone as IGP would be on seat and a subordinate had the audacity to take such a decision on such a high profile incident without authorisation from the IGP who ordinarily should have the last say on such a matter. This type of behaviour clearly shows that our system is not healthy. “Something is wrong somewhere. There is a gap somewhere. I wholly support the decision of the IGP to suspend the declaration by his subordinate.” Recall also that The Chairman of This Day Newspapers and Arise, Nduka Obaigbena

item.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. Violence may suppress voter turnout The INEC chairman identified three major consequences of political violence for the electoral process, including voter suppression, threats to the safety of electoral personnel and the possibility of post-election violence. item.description: …As Odii receives flag, promises economic revival By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwu Odii. Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates in the state. He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP stronghold since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party. The national chairman further alleged that the PDP won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that the party would reclaim its mandate in 2027. Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, he said, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty. He further alleged that the government spent less than its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. item.title: Kitto violence: Majority of victims suffer in silence – ISHRAI warns
item.description: .. Only 28% of victims report attacks, survey across six South-West states reveals By Chioma Obinna A growing pattern of online deception, blackmail, sexual exploitation and extortion is exposing young Nigerians and other vulnerable people to physical attacks, psychological trauma and even death, with a survey revealing that 71.3 per cent of respondents across six South-West states had experienced Kitto-related violence. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. The Improved Sexual Health and Rights Advocacy Initiative (ISHRAI), which disclosed the findings, raised the alarm over the trend, warning that victims were increasingly exposed to kidnapping, sexual abuse, blackmail, mob attacks and other forms of violence. The organisation called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, women and youth groups to intensify community awareness, protect vulnerable people and discourage public shaming, discrimination and jungle justice. Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement involving traditional and religious leaders, ISHRAI’s Programme Manager, Mrs Sophia Lawal, said community leaders must be equipped with the knowledge and referral mechanisms to identify cases of Kitto-related violence and respond appropriately. Lawal said the engagement brought together 20 traditional and religious leaders, including women leaders, to deliberate on the threats facing marginalised people and develop community-based responses. “It’s very important that we have community members, that’s the religious, traditional leaders, and also the women leaders, to have conversations around kitto violence that affects marginalized people in Nigeria,” she said. “And we cannot address these issues without having the right people in the room to deliberate on this matter together so that they are equipped with the right, with the knowledge to actually handle such cases when they are being reported or how to even identify such cases in their immediate community.” Providing details of the survey, an ISHRAI representative said 240 people were interviewed across the six South-West states, with 71.3 per cent indicating that they had experienced Kitto-related violence. He said the organisation’s intervention was aimed at reducing the practice through public education, early identification and effective community response. Explaining how perpetrators operate, he said many exploit social media to establish relationships with unsuspecting young men and women, build their confidence and lure them into physical meetings under false pretences. According to him, victims are sometimes encouraged to travel long distances, with perpetrators offering to pay their transport fares, book hotel accommodation or even arrange flights. item.title: ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt
item.description: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours of a postponement of the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise, confirming that it will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The exercise is scheduled to take place between 6:30am and 8:30am and will be monitored by government officials across various local government areas and local council development areas. The state government made the clarification on Thursday in a statement signed by Kunle Adeshina, Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The statement quoted the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen, as saying there was no basis for postponing the exercise. “There is no basis to cancel the monthly exercise which has become a rallying point for everyone to stay back and clean their neighbourhood,” Tajudeen said. He added that the November edition would be monitored across the state, as had become a tradition. According to the statement, the First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, will lead a team of government officials to monitor the exercise in Eti-Osa Local Government Area. Similarly, another team led by the Head of Service, Mr Olabode Agoro, will monitor activities in Coker-Aguda Local Council Development Area. Explaining the timing of the exercise, Tajudeen said the 6:30am to 8:30am schedule would allow residents to participate in the clean-up without disrupting other activities. He said the timeframe “gives enough room for any form of civic exercise to still be undertaken after the clean-up.” The permanent secretary urged Lagos residents to remain in their neighbourhoods and participate actively in the exercise. He also called on transport unions to use the opportunity to clean their parks and garages before resuming passenger operations at 8:30am. The state government reiterated its call for collective participation in maintaining environmental cleanliness across Lagos State. Vanguard News The post ‘Sanitation exercise to hold Saturday as scheduled’ – Lagos Govt appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections. The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party. The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties. She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state. Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence. She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement. The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace. She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements. In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections. They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities. The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections. item.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. item.title: Messi, Ronaldo could play together for first time at Tevez testimonial
item.description: Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them. The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United. Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires. Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid. If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side. Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand. item.title: 2027: Ogun ADC accepts Supreme Court ruling, backs Ogundipe as guber candidate
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accepted the Supreme Court ruling affirming Biodun Collins Ogundipe, popularly known as BCO, as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on aggrieved members to close ranks and work together for the success of the party at the polls. The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Executive Committee, local government area (LGA) chairmen, party leaders, elders and other stakeholders held on Thursday. The meeting, presided over by the State Chairman, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, considered the Supreme Court judgment alongside a letter dated November 23, 2026, from the party’s National Legal Adviser, which, according to the state chapter, reinforced the need for the party to operate within the provisions of the law. In a communiqué issued at the end of the meeting, the Ogun ADC said it had resolved to accept the apex court’s decision without prejudice and recognise Ogundipe as the party’s duly affirmed governorship candidate in the state. The party described its position as a demonstration of respect for the rule of law and the need to preserve the party’s unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. The development is expected to provide a fresh direction for the party’s preparations in Ogun State, particularly against the backdrop of leadership and governorship candidacy disputes that had generated disagreements among members. The communiqué further disclosed that Otunba Jimi Adebisi Lawal (JAL) and members of his campaign council had pledged their commitment to supporting the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, as well as all the party’s candidates in Ogun State. According to the communiqué, the party leadership has resolved to mobilise its entire political structure across the state to ensure victory for its candidates in the forthcoming elections. It said the mobilisation drive would extend across all levels of the party, including the state, local government, ward and polling unit structures. The party also reaffirmed its commitment to working collectively for the success of its candidates contesting the presidential, governorship, senatorial, Federal House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections. It added that political activities would be intensified in the months ahead to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, expand its support base and consolidate its electoral prospects ahead of 2027. Speaking on the need for reconciliation, Soluade appealed to party members, leaders and stakeholders to put aside their differences and unite behind the party’s collective ambition. He urged party loyalists and political stakeholders to shun bickering, divisive tendencies and unnecessary internal disagreements, emphasising that unity and cooperation were essential to the ADC’s success. item.title: Gbajabiamila leads Tinubu’s delegation to IBB, Abdulsalami
item.description: Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Femi Gbajabiamila, on Thursday led a presidential delegation to Minna, Niger State, to pay courtesy visits to former military Heads of State, Generals Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar. Gbajabiamila disclosed this in a statement, saying the visit was undertaken at the directive of President Tinubu to convey his goodwill and best wishes to the two elder statesmen. He said the delegation was warmly received by both former leaders, who appeared well and in high spirits during the visits. According to him, Babangida expressed satisfaction with the Tinubu administration’s performance, reaffirmed his support for the President and wished him success. Abdulsalami, on his part, commended the administration’s performance and thanked Tinubu for remembering the former leaders despite the demands of the ongoing election campaign. Gbajabiamila described the two former leaders as important figures in Nigeria’s history, noting that their experience and counsel remained invaluable to the country. “These are men who occupy major chapters in Nigeria’s history and their counsel remains invaluable,” he said. He added that the President was pleased with their support and expressed optimism about their continued backing in the coming elections. The visits come amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties and their candidates intensify consultations and mobilise support across the country. Babangida, who ruled Nigeria from 1985 to 1993, remains one of the country’s most influential former military leaders, while Abdulsalami, who assumed power in June 1998, oversaw the transition programme that ushered in the Fourth Republic in May 1999.

item.title: NAF: Tinubu Approves ₦100m, Houses For Families Of Air Crash Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. item.title: ORLSON seeks improved hearing care, specialist training as ENT experts meet in Kano
item.description: The Otorhinolaryngological Society of Nigeria (ORLSON) has called for urgent government intervention to address critical gaps in ear and hearing healthcare services across the country, citing inadequate infrastructure, shortage of specialists, rising cost of treatment and limited access to modern medical technologies. The call formed part of resolutions reached at the end of the Society’s 34th Annual General Meeting and Scientific Conference held from November 18 to 21 at the Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria (MAAUN), Kano. The resolutions are contained in a communique issued at the end of the conference and signed by ORLSON outgoing President, Professor Aliyu Mohammed Kodiya, and the outgoing Secretary, Dr Enema J. Amodu. The conference, which was held under the theme, “Advancing Otological Services in Nigeria: Bridging Gaps in Infrastructure, Training and Service Delivery,” brought together ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialists, resident doctors, audiologists, nurses, speech and language professionals, researchers, academics, healthcare administrators, development partners and industry stakeholders from within and outside Nigeria. A communiqué issued at the end of the four-day gathering highlighted growing concerns about the burden of preventable ear diseases and hearing loss in Nigeria and emphasized the need for a coordinated national response to improve access to quality ear and hearing care services. Wide-ranging deliberations The conference featured scientific presentations, panel discussions, workshops and stakeholder engagements that focused on various aspects of otorhinolaryngology, including otology, audiology, paediatric ENT practice, rhinology, laryngology and head and neck surgery. Participants examined challenges confronting hearing healthcare services in Nigeria and reviewed recent developments in clinical practice, training and research. As part of activities marking the conference, delegates paid courtesy visits to the management of the Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria, Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital and the Emir of Kano. The event was officially declared open by a representative of the Kano State Government, while participants also reviewed the progress of the professional body and conducted elections that produced a new National Officers Committee. ORLSON further used the occasion to showcase activities of its Abuja Secretariat and highlight ongoing efforts aimed at strengthening its digital platforms and institutional structures. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit.
